docs.title: Description
docs.text:
a VR-Lab for Simulation-based Learning.

Va.Si.Li-Lab is a Unity framework for collaborative, multi-user VR with customisable avatars and environments. It was established in DigiTeLL and is used in several projects. Systems built on it, such as InterView for VR survey interviews, are listed under Systems.

docs.title: Systems using Va.Si.Li-Lab
docs.text:
A list of Systems built on Va.Si.Li-Lab, as modules of this repository or as separate applications. Papers and BibTeX are listed under Publications.

System What it does Paper Part of InterView VR interviews: a participant in VR, the interviewer in a web browser Preprint FACES ReEmote Emotion representation for avatars and their environment XR Salento 2026 (accepted) FACES Va.Si.Li-ES Event system: triggers, environment and weather changes, voting and feedback HT '24 This repository (Assets/Lab/EventSystem) VR-ParlExplorer Plenary debates in VR with chatbot members of parliament HT '25 News in Time and Space Geospatial hypertext: global news events on a virtual globe NRHM 2025 Viki LibraRy A collaborative VR library for browsing and reading hypertext NRHM 2025 Semantic Scene Builder Text-to-3D scene generation, edited in VR HCII 2023 ViCom FraGA Frankfurt VR Gesture–Speech Alignment corpus, recorded in Va.Si.Li-Lab SemDial 2025 ViCom

docs.title: InterView
docs.text:
A platform for VR survey interviews. The participant wears a headset and sits across from the interviewer's avatar; the interviewer works from an ordinary browser. Speech, gaze, posture, hand movement, facial expression and the answers are captured on a shared clock. InterView adds a WebRTC media layer (Janus), a browser-based interviewer console and a token-driven session model to Va.Si.Li-Lab.

  • Platform documentation: texttechnologylab.github.io/InterView
  • VR client setup: InterView VR Client
  • Paper: InterView: Towards a Unified VR-Capable Interview Environment

docs.title: ReEmote
docs.text: Extends the face and hand tracking of Va.Si.Li-Lab with schema-based emotion mappings that affect both avatars and their environments, so users and virtual agents share one emotional expression space. Paper: ReEmote.

docs.title: Va.Si.Li-ES
docs.text: The event system of Va.Si.Li-Lab. Events are created and serialised at run time and change situational and environmental parameters (weather, objects, triggers); users are informed and can take part through voting and feedback. It ships as its own package, see Assets/Lab/EventSystem/README.md. Paper: Va.Si.Li-ES.

docs.title: VR-ParlExplorer
docs.text: A plugin for Va.Si.Li-Lab that virtualises plenary debates: users interact with virtual members of parliament through LLM-based chatbots. Paper: VR-ParlExplorer.

docs.title: News in Time and Space
docs.text: News in Time and Space (NiTS) organises news articles (currently based on GDELT) as a geospatial hypertext on a virtual globe, where users visualise, filter and explore global events and trends. Paper: Geo-spatial hypertext in virtual reality.

docs.title: Viki LibraRy
docs.text: A dynamically built library in VR that visualises hypertext systems, with an emphasis on collaborative reading and spatial recall. Paper: Viki LibraRy.

docs.title: Semantic Scene Builder
docs.text: A VR-based text-to-3D framework: scenes are generated from annotated text descriptions and corrected by grabbing and moving objects instead of editing annotations. Paper: Semantic Scene Builder.

docs.title: FraGA
docs.text: The Frankfurt VR Gesture–Speech Alignment corpus, used for multimodal analyses of head and hand movements in dialogue. Paper: FraGA.

docs.title: Adding Scenes
docs.text: To connect a scene via MetaStart, you must first add the scene to the Unity project and then to the MongoDB database.

docs.title: Create a new Scene
docs.text:
• Place your scenes in a folder of your own project, e.g. Assets/Scenes, not inside Assets/Lab.
  • The easiest start is a copy of the Example sample scene (see Special Scenes). It already contains the Social Network Scene prefab for networking.
  • Don't add a player or camera: the player comes from MetaStart.
  • Add a GameObject for each spawn point and name it like the role's spawnPosition (e.g. DefaultSpawn).
  • Add the scene to the build profile (File > Build Profiles > Scene List), after MetaStart.

docs.title: Debug Scene without MetaStart
docs.text: To test a scene on its own, temporarily add the prefabs MetaPlayer2.0 and AvatarSdkManagerStyle2Meta (from the Meta Avatars Sample Scenes, folder Common/Prefabs/AvatarSdkManager/Recommended), as MetaStart does. Rename the manager to AvatarSdkManagerMeta: the avatar scripts look it up by that name. Remove both again before building.

docs.title: Add Scene to the Database
docs.text:
The Scene must be added to the database to be accessible via MetaStart. There are two ways to do this:

  • Via the Database API (recommended). The Database API now has endpoints for creating scenes, roles, levels and their locales, so you don't need direct database access - just an API key. Start there; the walkthrough builds exactly the structure documented below, one call at a time.
  • Directly in MongoDB. As a student, ask your corresponding supervisor to add the scene for you. Scenes are stored in the scenarios collection, in the structure below.

This is the structure of a scene, as GET /scene returns it and as the client reads it (ApiScene in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/SceneManagement/SceneManagerTypes.cs):

Field Meaning name, shortName Name in the scene selector, and a short version where space is limited author Author of the scenario internalName Name of the Unity scene enabled Visible in MetaStart roles Roles by identifier (your own key, e.g. interviewee) roles.<id>.mode player or spectator (webcam exists but is not used by the client yet) roles.<id>.spawnPosition Name of the GameObject in the scene the role spawns at roles.<id>.maxCount Maximum number of players with this role roles.<id>.admin The admin starts and ends the levels roles.<id>.restrictions Restrictions of the role, e.g. blur roles.<id>.locales.<lang> name and description of the role per language (EN, DE) levels The stages of the scenario, in order levels[].delay Stops the level after n minutes (null: no limit) levels[].roleDescriptions.<id>.locales.<lang> What the role does in this level

The example below defines the InterView sample scene: an interviewee in VR who starts and ends the level, and an optional spectator. The spawn points DefaultSpawn and spectator exist in that scene.

Example Scene Entry
{
  "name": "InterView Sample",
  "shortName": "InterView",
  "author": "Jane Doe",
  "internalName": "InterView",
  "enabled": true,
  "roles": {
    "interviewee": {
      "mode": "player",
      "spawnPosition": "DefaultSpawn",
      "maxCount": 1,
      "admin": true,
      "restrictions": [],
      "locales": {
        "EN": { "name": "Interviewee", "description": ["Answer the interviewer's questions."] },
        "DE": { "name": "Befragte Person", "description": ["Beantworte die Fragen der interviewenden Person."] }
      }
    },
    "spectator": {
      "mode": "spectator",
      "spawnPosition": "spectator",
      "maxCount": 1,
      "admin": false,
      "restrictions": [],
      "locales": {
        "EN": { "name": "Spectator", "description": ["Watch the interview."] },
        "DE": { "name": "Beobachtung", "description": ["Beobachte das Interview."] }
      }
    }
  },
  "levels": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "delay": null,
      "roleDescriptions": {
        "interviewee": { "locales": { "EN": { "description": ["Interview"] }, "DE": { "description": ["Interview"] } } },
        "spectator": { "locales": { "EN": { "description": ["Observe"] }, "DE": { "description": ["Beobachten"] } } }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: InterView VR Client
docs.text:
InterView is a platform for conducting survey interviews in virtual reality, built on Va.Si.Li-Lab. The participant wears a headset and sits across from the interviewer's avatar; the interviewer works from an ordinary web browser.

This page covers setting up the VR client - the Unity side. The platform itself, its services and their deployment are documented separately:

Platform documentation

Architecture, server setup, Janus, coturn, Ubiq, the logging API and the web client are documented at texttechnologylab.github.io/InterView.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Unity project set up as described in Setting Up Va.Si.Li-Lab, with Android support for Quest builds
  • A running InterView backend - see the InterView Setup Guide
  • A Meta Quest headset in developer mode

docs.title: What the client connects to
docs.text:
Four independent services, all configured in the endpoints file (Assets/Resources/VasiliEndpoints.asset). Each can fail without the others noticing.

Service Purpose Endpoints field Janus Audio/video and the control data channel janus, iceServers Ubiq VR room and avatar state ubiqServer Logging API Tracking data and events api Questionnaire The survey instrument questionnaire

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The InterView sample scenes are in Assets/Lab/Core/Samples/Scenes: InterViewStart (token entry, holds the InterviewTokenManager), InterView (the interview room, holds the WebCamClient) and InterViewReturn. Add all three to the build profile, InterViewStart first, and check the components below.

docs.title: WebCamClient
docs.text:
The Janus client. Publishes local audio and video, subscribes to the interviewer's feed, and hosts the textroom data channel that carries chat, answer options, gaze updates and the recording signal. Its server comes from janus in the endpoints: use wss://janus.<your-domain>, the TLS endpoint of your reverse proxy, not Janus's own port. iceServers must match the TURN server the backend uses.

Field Value Notes SubProtocol janus-protocol Leave unchanged RecordingPath /mnt/recordings/ Path inside the Janus container; the room ID is appended automatically captureWidth / captureHeight 854 × 480 maxBitrate / minBitrate 1000000 / 250000 maxFramerate 24

docs.title: InterviewTokenManager
docs.text:
Holds the participant token across scene loads and derives every identifier from it, so the headset and the interviewer's browser meet without a coordination step.

The questionnaire URL is questionnaire in the endpoints. The token is appended as ?token=…&room=…. The follow-up questionnaire that the interviewer can send afterwards is followupQuestionnaire.

token ──┬─→ RoomId         (Janus room ID)
        ├─→ UbiqRoomName   = "interview-{token}"
        └─→ BrowserUrl     = {questionnaire}?token={token}&room={token}

The room ID is the token parsed as an integer when it is all digits, and otherwise a DJB2 hash (seed 5381, multiplier 33), absolute value, minimum 1.

This derivation exists twice and must stay identical

The same function is implemented in the web client as roomIdFromString() in js/state.js. If the two ever disagree, the interviewer and the participant join different rooms - each waits alone, and no error is shown anywhere. Change both or neither.

docs.title: Ubiq connection
docs.text: Set ubiqServer in the endpoints to a Ubiq connection definition with your Ubiq host and its published TCP port (16485 in the default deployment).

docs.title: Logging API
docs.text:
Set api in the endpoints to your Database API URL.

A wrong API address loses the whole session, silently

Logging failures do not interrupt an interview. The session looks completely normal and records nothing. Verify that data is arriving before a participant sits down, not afterwards.

docs.title: Building for Quest
docs.text:
1. Switch the build target to Android.
  2. Resolve any outstanding items in the Meta Project Setup Tool.
  3. Build and deploy to the headset.

docs.title: Pre-session checklist
docs.text:
• janus reachable from the headset's network
  • TURN credentials current and matching the server
  • Ubiq host and port correct
  • api points at the running Database API
  • questionnaire points at the correct questionnaire
  • A full test interview completed, with data confirmed in the database

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptoms and their usual causes - connection failures, missing media, data channel problems - are collected in the InterView operations guide.

docs.title: Meta Avatar
docs.text:
Instead of the Ubiq avatars, we are using the Meta Avatar system. The avatars have the following advantages:

  • Diverse cast of pre-built avatars + customization options
  • Visualisation of Hand- and Finger-Tracking
  • Visualisation of Eye-Tracking
  • Visualisation of Facial Expressions

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The Meta Avatars SDK (com.meta.xr.sdk.avatars, 40.0.1) is installed from the Unity registry as a dependency of Va.Si.Li-Lab. Its Sample Scenes sample must be imported, because Va.Si.Li-Lab uses SampleAvatarEntity and the AvatarSdkManagerStyle2Meta prefab from it (in MetaStart, renamed to AvatarSdkManagerMeta, the name the avatar scripts look up), see Setting Up.

The avatar scripts of Va.Si.Li-Lab are in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/MetaAvatars. The local avatar is driven by MetaAvatarInput on the player.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Meta Avatar Documentation
  • Meta Avatars SDK on the Unity registry (Package Manager > Unity Registry > Meta Avatars SDK)

docs.title: Player Controller
docs.text: The player is the prefab MetaPlayer2.0 in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Prefabs. It is built from Meta XR Building Blocks and works with controllers and hand tracking.

docs.title: How it is used
docs.text:
• Only the MetaStart scene contains the player. DontDestroyOnLoad keeps it alive when a scenario scene is loaded, so scenario scenes must not contain their own player or camera.
  • When the role or scene changes, PlayerSpawnManager moves the player to the role's spawn point: a GameObject whose name matches the role's spawnPosition in the scene definition. Afterwards MenuRequestManager opens the social menu.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Object Contents MetaPlayer2.0 (root) OVRPlayerController + CharacterController (thumbstick movement, 45° snap turn, gravity), PlayerSpawnManager, MenuRequestManager, DontDestroyOnLoad, DistanceObjectDesktopUser [BuildingBlock] Camera Rig OVRCameraRig and OVRManager: head, eye and hand anchors [BuildingBlock] Interaction Interaction SDK rig: hand and controller interactions (grab, distance grab, poke, ray), synthetic hands, the Locomotor (teleport arc, turning, step locomotion with hands) and the eye-gaze ray (EyeGazePointerPose) Meta Avatar Input (OVR) MetaAvatarInput: feeds head and hand tracking into the local Meta avatar BlurEffect Blurred vision for roles with the blur restriction

docs.title: Movement scripts
docs.text:
All in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/Movement:

Script Purpose PlayerSpawnManager Moves the local player to the role's spawn point after a role or scene change MovementLock Locks movement while the player's status is waiting and lifts the blur restriction meanwhile TeleportOnTrigger Teleports a player to a target when they enter a trigger collider ContinousMovementEventBroadcaster Turns a thumbstick axis into continuous locomotion events

docs.title: Input
docs.text: The project uses the Input System only (Player Settings > Active Input Handling). For buttons that should work with controllers, hand tracking and a desktop keyboard alike, use VaSiLi.Helper.LabInput (e.g. LabInput.PrimaryDown). For controller- or hand-specific input use OVRInput and OVRHand, see Meta input actions.

docs.title: Adding interactions to objects
docs.text:
The player already has all interactors, so an object only needs an interactable:

  1. Select the GameObject, right-click and choose Interaction SDK and the interaction you want (hand grab, distance grab, poke, ray grab, ...).
  2. If the object has no Collider or Rigidbody yet, click Create in the dialog. This adds an ISDK_... child object.

Don't put every interaction type on one object. If only part of a large object should be interactable, add the interactable to that part only. More: Interaction SDK overview.

docs.title: Teleporting in a scene
docs.text: The Locomotor handles teleporting and turning. To make a floor teleportable, add a teleport interactable to it, for example with Add Teleport Quick Action from the Interaction SDK, or copy HotspotVoidFloor and NavMeshHotspotWalkable from Meta's locomotion sample scene (and CollidersTeleportBlocker to stop teleports through walls). You may need to adjust the floor's height so it doesn't block the arc.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Meta Interaction SDK
  • Hand tracking

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text: git clone https://github.com/texttechnologylab/Va.Si.Li-Lab.git

docs.title: Open the Project with UnityHub
docs.text: Unity Hub downloads the correct Unity version (6000.3) for you. Add Android Build Support if you want to build for Meta Quest headsets.

docs.title: Import the required samples
docs.text:
Va.Si.Li-Lab uses code and prefabs from two package samples. Import them in Window > Package Manager (select the package, Samples tab, Import). Until then you get compile errors such as SampleAvatarEntity could not be found.

Package Sample Meta Avatars SDK Sample Scenes Ubiq Demo (XRI)

The Meta Avatars sample doesn't compile against Platform SDK 207 ('CAPI' does not exist in the namespace 'Oculus.Platform'). In Assets/Samples/Meta Avatars SDK/40.0.1/Sample Scenes/Scripts/Utility/AvatarEditorUtils.cs replace the line var result = new Request<…>(Oculus.Platform.CAPI.ovr_Avatar_LaunchAvatarEditor((IntPtr)options)); with:

var result = Oculus.Platform.Avatar.LaunchAvatarEditor(options);

Also import TextMesh Pro Essential Resources when Unity asks.

docs.title: Quick-start
docs.text:
1. Run Tools > Va.Si.Li > Create Endpoints Config. This creates Assets/Resources/VasiliEndpoints.asset, which holds the addresses of all servers (Ubiq server, Database API, speech, chatbot, WebRTC). Point it to your own server installation. For quick tests, set Ubiq Server to the Nexus Connection Definition provided by UCL (features that need our backend will be missing).
  2. Open the MetaStart scene in Assets/Lab/Core/Samples/Scenes and press Play. Without a headset, use the Meta XR Simulator.

docs.title: Import as Unity Package
docs.text:
Unity can't install git dependencies of a package, so add these to your project's Packages/manifest.json yourself:

"com.ucl.ubiq": "https://github.com/UCL-VR/ubiq.git#upm-unity-v1.0.0-pre.16",
"com.tlabaltoh.webview": "https://github.com/TLabAltoh/TLabWebView.git#upm",
"com.tlabaltoh.vkeyborad": "https://github.com/TLabAltoh/TLabVKeyborad.git#upm",
"org.texttechnologylab.vasili": "https://github.com/texttechnologylab/Va.Si.Li-Lab.git#upm"

The event system (Va.Si.Li-ES) is a separate, optional package: "org.texttechnologylab.vasili-es": "https://github.com/texttechnologylab/Va.Si.Li-Lab.git#upm-eventsystem". All other dependencies (Meta XR SDKs, XR Interaction Toolkit, WebRTC, ...) are installed automatically.

Then:

  1. Import the required samples and apply the AvatarEditorUtils.cs fix.
  2. Import the Va.Si.Li-Lab samples (Package Manager > Va.Si.Li-Lab > Samples) for the scenes.
  3. Fix the remaining issues listed in Meta XR Project Setup Tool.
  4. Set Player Settings > Active Input Handling to Input System Package (New).
  5. Continue with the quick-start.

docs.title: Special Scenes
docs.text: The sample scenes are in Assets/Lab/Core/Samples/Scenes. When Va.Si.Li-Lab is installed as a package, import them via Package Manager > Va.Si.Li-Lab > Samples.

docs.title: MetaStart
docs.text: Starting scene for every experiment. It contains the player, the scene selector and the network connection. Here the user selects an avatar and joins a scenario.

docs.title: MetaReturn
docs.text: Helper scene the user returns to when disconnecting from a scenario (instead of MetaStart). Some scripts that would otherwise cause problems are removed here.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: Tutorial scene to get familiar with the controls. Can be started from MetaStart.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Minimal scenario scene (networking and a box of pens) to copy when adding a scene.

docs.title: InterViewStart, InterView, InterViewReturn
docs.text:
The scenes of InterView, used instead of MetaStart/MetaReturn for VR interviews:

  • InterViewStart: the participant enters the interview token (InterviewTokenManager).
  • InterView: the interview room with the interviewee's seat, a mirror (self-view), the in-world browser for the questionnaire and the WebRTC (Janus) connection to the interviewer's browser.
  • InterViewReturn: shown after the interview.

See InterView VR Client for their configuration.

docs.title: Bots
docs.text: Va.Si.Li-Lab has LLM-based agents that users talk to by voice and that can act in the scene through tools. The code is in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/LLM (namespace VaSiLi.Llm). The agents need two backend services: vr-agent (agent in the endpoints), which talks to the LLM, and tts-stt (speechSynthesis) for speech in and out.

docs.title: Prefabs
docs.text:
Both are samples (Assets/Lab/Core/Samples/Objects/Prefabs):

Prefab Contents AgentToolkit One per scene: AgentManager (creates the agents), AgentToolProvider (collects the tools), PlayerMicListener (push-to-talk) and ToolExamples AgentBot One agent: the bot model, AgentInstance, ChatAPI (speech in and out) and its UI (AgentActivatorUI, ToolWhitelistUI, ToolLogUI)

MetaStart contains an AgentToolkit; AgentManager spawns AgentBot instances from it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. AgentManager creates the agents listed in its Agents field: for each it instantiates the AgentBot prefab at the given position and registers the agent with the agent service (/createAgent). The system prompt is the agent's Persona followed by the tool-call instructions. Set the list on the AgentToolkit instance of each scene.
  2. The user activates an agent (AgentActivatorUI) and talks to it. PlayerMicListener records while A (or the right index pinch, or V on a keyboard) is held and passes the recording to every active agent. It only records while at least one agent is active.
  3. ChatAPI transcribes the audio (speechSynthesis/whisperx) and sends the text to the agent (agent/chat).
  4. The agent answers with text, which ChatAPI speaks (speechSynthesis/tts), or with a tool call.
  5. AgentInstance runs tool calls the user has allowed for that agent (ToolWhitelistUI) and logs them (ToolLogUI).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
A tool is any method marked with [AgentTool] on a MonoBehaviour in the scene. AgentToolProvider finds them by reflection and sends their descriptions to the agent service (/toolDescriptions):

using UnityEngine;
using VaSiLi.Llm;

public class LampTools : MonoBehaviour
{
    public Light lamp;

    [AgentTool("switch_lamp", "Call when the user wants the lamp switched on or off.")]
    public string SwitchLamp(bool on)
    {
        lamp.enabled = on;
        return on ? "The lamp is on" : "The lamp is off";
    }
}

Parameters can be string, int, float, double, bool and Vector3; for other types the agent passes the name of an earlier tool call, and that call's return value is used. The returned string goes back to the agent as the result. ToolExamples has more examples (spawning prefabs, changing colours and textures). Components that implement IAgentContextInfo add information about the scene to the agent's context.

docs.title: Chatbot module
docs.text: Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/Modules/Chatbot is an older, simpler voice chatbot: ChatBotManager sends recorded audio to speech/query and plays the answer, ChatBotSelectButton picks the chatbot. It uses the speech service.

docs.title: Endpoints Configuration
docs.text:
All server addresses of the client live in one asset, VasiliEndpoints (Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/Networking/VasiliEndpoints.cs). It is loaded from any Resources folder by the name VasiliEndpoints.

The repository doesn't ship one. Create yours with Tools > Va.Si.Li > Create Endpoints Config, which writes Assets/Resources/VasiliEndpoints.asset. Until then, every service falls back to localhost and a warning is logged at start-up.

Don't commit your endpoints file to a public repository

It contains your server addresses and TURN credentials. Keep it in a private folder or repository.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Used by Without it ubiqServer 127.0.0.1:8009 (TCP) VasiliServerConnection on the RoomClient of the Social Network Scene prefab No multiplayer room api http://localhost:8000 Database API: scene definitions (SceneManager), logging, tutorials, connection status No scenes in MetaStart, nothing is logged speech http://localhost:8001 speech2text: MicrophoneListener (/whisper); chatbot host: ChatBotManager (/query). Both are expected at this address No speech input agent http://localhost:8002 vr-agent: AgentManager, AgentInstance, AgentToolProvider, ChatAPI (/chat), see Bots No agents speechSynthesis http://localhost:8003 tts-stt: ChatAPI transcription (/whisperx) and text-to-speech (/tts) Agents don't hear or speak shapeNet http://localhost:8004 ShapeNet object search and download (ShapeNetInterface) No ShapeNet objects eventTemplates http://localhost:4567 Event System templates (/defaultTemplates) No saved or default event systems questionnaire (empty) InterView: questionnaire page opened in the in-world browser (InterviewTokenManager) Empty browser in InterView followupQuestionnaire (empty) InterView: follow-up questionnaire the interviewer sends to the interviewee (WebCamClient follow-up button; the interview token is appended) The follow-up button logs a warning and sends nothing janus ws://localhost:8188 WebRTC (Janus) for InterView and the webcam screen (WebCamClient) No audio/video with the interviewer iceServers (empty) STUN/TURN servers for WebRTC. Leave username/credential empty for STUN WebRTC only works on the same network

Base URLs are written without a trailing slash. Use wss:// for Janus behind a TLS reverse proxy.

docs.title: In code
docs.text:
using VaSiLi.Networking;

string url = VasiliEndpoints.Current.api + "/logging/status";

VasiliEndpoints.Current is loaded once and cached. To add a new service, add a field with a localhost default and a tooltip to VasiliEndpoints, and read it through Current. Don't hard-code hosts: Tools/Publish/check-public.sh reports them.

docs.title: Event System (Va.Si.Li-ES)
docs.text:
The event system lets users build event systems at run time, inside VR: triggers (an area is entered, an object is used, a timer runs out) start events (spawn, move or delete objects, teleport players, change the weather, start a vote or show feedback). Event systems can be saved as templates and loaded automatically when a scene starts. It is described in the paper Va.Si.Li-ES.

The code is in Assets/Lab/EventSystem (assembly Vasili.EventSystem). As a Unity package it is installed separately from the core, see Setting Up.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Concept Interface Implementations (Runtime/...) Event system IEventSystem EventSystem: holds triggers and events in numbered groups, can be repeatable Trigger ITrigger Triggers/AreaTrigger, InteractionTrigger, TimeTrigger Event IEvent Events/ObjectSpawningEvent, ObjectMovingEvent, ObjectDestructionEvent, PlayerTeleportationEvent, WeatherEvent, VotingEvent, FeedbackEvent, FollowingEventSystemEvent (starts another event system) Modifier IModifier Modifiers/Modifier_Gravity, _Jump, _Speed, _Weather, _Zoom, _Map, _Admin; Modefier_Handler switches the modifiers in its Modifier_Container on or off according to the scene's ModifierSettings

When all triggers of a group have fired, the events of that group run. Group 0 is shared: its triggers are required by every group, and its events run whenever any group fires. A repeatable event system resets its triggers afterwards, otherwise it deletes itself. Triggers and events serialise themselves to JSON (createJson), which is how templates are stored.

docs.title: Building blocks
docs.text:
Prefab Purpose Manager/EventSystemManager Menu that lists the scene's event systems, loads templates and the scene's default event systems on start Factory/EventSystemFactory Creates one event system with its triggers and events MarkerTool/MarkerTool Tool for placing triggers and events in the scene EnvironmentSystem/Weather/Weather_Controller Weather (rain, snow, thunderstorm) used by WeatherEvent and Modifier_Weather VotingSystem/Voting_Controller Votes (yes/no or single choice) used by VotingEvent FeedbackSystem/Notification Manager, FeedbackWindow Notifications and feedback used by FeedbackEvent EventSystemPrefabs/* Ready-made items: binoculars, jump and sprint shoes, map, weather clouds, environment changer

To use it in a scene, add the EventSystemManager prefab (and the controllers for the events you need) to the scene.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: EventSystemManager reads and writes templates at eventTemplates + "/defaultTemplates" (see Endpoints). A template belongs to the scene whose name it stores; templates of the current scene are offered in the template panel, and default ones are created when the scene loads.

docs.title: Extending
docs.text:
• New trigger: a MonoBehaviour implementing ITrigger. Call notifySystem() when it fires, and return its state from getState().
  • New event: a MonoBehaviour implementing IEvent. Do the work in trigger(), show what will happen in previewOn()/previewOff().
  • New modifier: implement IModifier and add it to the Modifier_Container used by Modefier_Handler. The scene's ModifierSettings decide whether it is allowed and clamp its value.

Both triggers and events need createJson(groupID) so they can be saved in templates.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Va.Si.Li-Lab records what happens in a session (movement, gaze, faces, hands, interactions, audio) and sends it to the Database API, which stores it in MongoDB. The data model behind it is described in A Multimodal Data Model for Simulation-Based Learning with Va.Si.Li-Lab.

The code is in Assets/Lab/Core/Runtime/Scripts/Logging. The address comes from api in the endpoints configuration.

docs.title: MetaDataLogger
docs.text:
MetaDataLogger on the Social Network Scene prefab collects the data of the local player and sends it in batches:

Route (api + ...) Content /logging/playerLogIn A player joins /logging/playerRoleLogIn A player takes a role /logging/levelChange The admin changes the level /logging/player Head, hand and body tracking; with Meta avatars also eyes, face and fingers (metaMessage) /logging/object Positions of logged objects /logging/special Button presses and spawned objects /logging/logMisc Other events

The message types are in DataLoggerTypes.cs. How the API splits them into collections is described in the Database API documentation.

Logging failures don't stop a session

If the API can't be reached, the session continues normally and nothing is stored. Check that data arrives (e.g. api + /logging/status, shown by ConnectionStatusMonitor) before a study session starts.

docs.title: Other loggers
docs.text: Component Purpose FileLogger Writes the JSON messages to the local file system instead LogManager, Collectors/MovementLogCollector Collector-based logging (ILogCollector, IContinousLogCollector, IEventLogCollector) LogToScreen Shows Unity log output in VR DevLogConfig Disables per-log stack traces in development builds

docs.title: Experiment Visualization
docs.text:
In preparation

A new tool for analysing and visualising recorded experiments (audio transcription, tracking data) is in preparation and will be documented here once it is released. The previous Streamlit tools are no longer maintained.

docs.title: Simulations & Experiments Playback
docs.text:
Not available in the current version

The SimulationLoader scene and the Assets/Simulation_dev folder described here are not part of the current repository. A new replay tool is in preparation; until then this page documents the earlier one.

Simulations and Experiments performed using this project can be replayed using the following steps:

docs.title: Add Scenes to Build Setting
docs.text:
Scenes to be replayed and the SimulationLoader scene should be added to build setting.

  1. Open SimulationLoader scene located in Assets/Simulation_dev/Scenes.
  2. From File tab choose Build Settings....
  3. Add SimulationLoader scene to build by clicking Add Open Scenes.
  4. Make sure SimulationLoader scene is enabled using the toggle to its left side.
  5. Add and enable all scenes of the Simulations/Experiments to be replayed.

docs.title: Start Playback
docs.text: To start playback open and play SimulationLoader scene.

docs.title: Local Playback
docs.text:
Scene will search for previous Playbacks, if any has been saved.

Choose the scene, date and players to be replayed then click on Next.

docs.title: Online Playback
docs.text:
If no local data found, or if online data is preferred, using the Load Online Data toggle (Disabled by default) will connect to the server and retrieve information about Simulations and its data.

By online Playback the following options are available:

  • Keeping the chosen playbacks data if local instances of it are found, or Saving the chosen playbacks if no local data of it found using the Keep Json Copy toggle. Local data will be yellow colored by the list of players to choose from. (Enabled by default)
  • Use online data instead of local data of the chosen playbacks, if any local data found, using the Updated Info toggle. This will Replace local data if Keep Json Copy toggle is enabled. (Disabled by default)
  • Note:
    • Disabling Keep Json Copy will remove any local data, of the chosen playbacks only, saved previously.
    • Having Updated Info toggle enabled or disabled when no local data is found will have no different action and will load online data anyway.
    • If any local playbacks are found, it will be colored yellow and will say Json Available by the list of players to choose from.

After choosing players click on Next.

docs.title: Choosing Avatars
docs.text:
After choosing players and clicking Next, a new page is loaded with the name of chosen Scene, Instructions on how to control playback with keyboard and the ability to choose different avatars for each player.

Default avatars will be set according to the info retrieved online or from local data. If none found, Avatar Nr. 0 will be set as default.

Click on Load Scene to Start playback after all required data have been loaded.

docs.title: Playback Control
docs.text: There are several ways to control the playback:

docs.title: 3. Person Camera
docs.text:
• Arrow Keys: Horizontal & Vertical Rotation.
  • T,G: Zoom in/Out.
  • F,H: Next/Previous Player.
  • P: Pause Playbacks (Audio & Movement).
  • O: Change Audio Mode.
    • Global: Audio from all players will be heard. (Default)
    • Single: Audio only from the current chosen player.
  • Space: Take a Screenshot. Will be saved in screenshots folder.

docs.title: 1. Person Camera
docs.text:
• C: Activate/Disable 1. Person Camera.

Note: While in 1. Person Camera, no camera movements controls are available. This will imitate being in the perspective of the current player.

docs.title: Free Camera
docs.text:
• Q: Activate/Disable Free Camera.
  • Arrow Keys: Movement.
  • T,G: Vertical Rotation.
  • F,H: Horizontal Rotation.
  • Z,X: Height Control.
  • V,B: Jump to next player's position.

Note: Once activated, Camera will be positioned at a default location. Depending on the scene, this location might be far from players. using V,B will move Camera to the position of the next/previous player.

docs.title: Custom Inspector
docs.text: Another Option to Control Playback is through a custom inspector. When Playback starts, inside Hierarchy tab, click on Simulation(Clone) object under DontDestroyOnLoad. Custom inspector will be shown inside Inspector tab.

docs.title: Player Info
docs.text:
• Choosing players.
  • Loop Variable slider.
    • This will show in which frame, in regards to the current player's playback frame count, the current player is.
    • Changing the value by sliding or giving a valid number in the input field will pause the playback. Click Play or Apply to continue.
  • Audio Mode Switcher.
  • Back button to change chosen playbacks without the need to stop and replay the scene.
  • Play/Pause Playback.
  • Screenshot|. Take a screenshot | Open the folder, where all screenshots are saved.
  • Show/Hide Instructions Show Instructions of the keyboard controls.

docs.title: Weights Multiplier
docs.text:
• Face/Eye Weights: With a value between 0 and 2 to control the intensity of the Face/Eye pose for all playbacks.
  • Hand Pos. Senset.: With a value between 0.4 and 1.5. When the difference in vertical hand position between the current frame and the previous one is bigger than this value, the old value from the previous frame will be taken instead and ignore the current one, to avoid having hands in extreme positions. This can happen mostly when switching between Finger tracking and Controller tracking.
  • Voice Ind. Senset.: With a value between 0.0001 and 1. Controls the sensitivity of the voice indicator above each player's avatar. Higher values will require higher sounds to activate the indicator. By value 1 the voice indicator will mostly be disabled.

docs.title: Camera Control
docs.text:
• 1. Person view toggle to activate 1. Person Camera.
  • Free Camera toggle to activate Free Camera. This will show additional buttons underneath for movement control.
  • Rotation & Zoom Controls when Free Camera is disabled / Movement, Rotation & Height Controls When Free Camera is activated.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text: • Log chosen data to console.

docs.title: Time & Speed Slider
docs.text:
• Speed Slider: With a value between 0.1 and 2, will control the speed of all playbacks' movements and sounds.
  • Time Slider: Once selected or changed value, playbacks' movements and sounds will be paused. Unpause through inspector or keyboard P to continue.

docs.title: Record Playback
docs.text:
All playbacks can be recorded and exported as a video:

  • Add Recorder Window by navigating to Window tab then clicking General>Recorder>Recorder Window.
  • In Recorder Window choose desired settings then click START RECORDING and when finished STOP RECORDING.

Note: While Recording, Sounds from playbacks may not be heard through Unity, but it's all being recorded in the video.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Research projects in which Va.Si.Li-Lab is developed and used.

Project Funding Va.Si.Li-Lab is used for DigiTeLL Goethe University Frankfurt, Digital Teaching and Learning Lab Origin of Va.Si.Li-Lab: simulation-based learning in VR for teaching ViCom / GeMDiS DFG Priority Programme 2392 Visual Communication Gestures in dialogue: VR-based multimodal data collection (FraGA, Semantic Scene Builder) New Data Spaces / FACES DFG Priority Programme 2431 New Data Spaces Survey interviews in VR (InterView, ReEmote)

Systems built on Va.Si.Li-Lab are listed in Systems using Va.Si.Li-Lab.

docs.title: DigiTeLL 2022
docs.text:
(DigiTeLL)

The core of the project is the ‘Digital Teaching and Learning Lab’ (DigiTeLL), a virtual communication and collaboration space designed to enable permanent innovation loops. In the lab, teachers or student groups will network with each other and with central support structures as part of so-called partnerships in order to implement innovative development projects in courses. In particular, the teaching, learning and examination scenarios at Goethe University will be expanded to include digital instruments and innovative learning designs. Link

Project Link

docs.title: New Data Spaces
docs.text: New Data Spaces - DFG SPP 2431

docs.title: FACES
docs.text:
FACES (Feasibility, acceptance, and data quality of new multimodal surveys) is part of this SPP. Project website: texttechnologylab.github.io/FACES.

Conventional surveys record the answer and discard everything that produced it - the hesitation, the gaze, whether the question was understood at all. FACES asks whether conducting interviews in VR can retain that context, and whether the resulting data holds up: is a VR-mediated interview feasible, do respondents accept it, and is the data quality comparable to established modes?

The studies conducted in FACES are listed on the FACES website.

docs.title: InterView
docs.text:
The platform built to answer that question is InterView. A participant wears a VR headset and sits across from the interviewer's avatar in a shared virtual room; the interviewer works from an ordinary web browser. Speech, gaze, posture, hand movement, facial expression and the answers themselves are all captured on a shared clock.

InterView is built on Va.Si.Li-Lab and adds a WebRTC media layer, a browser-based interviewer console, and a token-driven session model. Avatar emotions come from ReEmote. Both are listed under Systems using Va.Si.Li-Lab, their papers under Publications.

InterView has its own documentation

Architecture, the full deployment guide, and reference documentation for every service - Janus, coturn, Ubiq, the logging API and the web client - are at texttechnologylab.github.io/InterView.

Setting up the VR client is documented here, in InterView VR Client.

Repository Contains InterView Deployment stack and platform documentation Va.Si.Li-Lab The VR client faces-website Web client Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend Ubiq server and logging API sources

docs.title: ViCom
docs.text:
ViCom (Visual Communication) - DFG Priority Programme 2392

ViCom investigates the special features and linguistic significance of visual communication. This comprises sign languages as fully developed natural languages which exclusively rely on the visual channel for communication, but also visual means that enhance spoken language such as gestures. It aims at disclosing the specific characteristics of the visual modality as a communication channel and its interaction with other channels (especially the auditory channel) to develop a comprehensive theoretical linguistic model of human communication and its cognitive foundations.

docs.title: GeMDiS
docs.text: GeMDiS (Virtual Reality Sustained Multimodal Distributional Semantics for Gestures in Dialogue) is part of ViCom.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
A scenario is a scene plus its scene definition (roles, levels, spawn points). Scenario scenes made for studies are kept in the projects that run them; the public repository contains the sample scenes:

Scene Purpose Example Minimal scenario to start a new scene from InterViewStart, InterView, InterViewReturn InterView: token entry, the interview room (seat, mirror, in-world browser, WebRTC connection to the interviewer) and the end screen Tutorial Learn the controls

docs.title: MongoDB
docs.text:
We use a MongoDB to store the experiments and the recorded data of all participants. It is written to exclusively by the Database API - nothing else connects to it directly.

Collections, indexes and timestamps

The collections the API creates, the indexes it declares on startup, and the difference between the client-side localTime and the server-assigned serverTime are documented at Data Model in the backend documentation.

That distinction matters for analysis: serverTime is stamped when a batched request arrives, so every sample in one batch shares it. Use localTime for alignment within a client.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
You can run a MongoDB instance using Docker. You should adapt all paths and logins to your needs.

example.yaml to create a MongoDB container
version: '3'
services:
  mongodb_container:
    image: mongo:latest
    container_name: vasililab_mongodb
    hostname: mongodb
    restart: always
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: root #(1)
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: root
    ports:
      - "27017:27017"
    volumes:
      - /vol/mongoVaSiLiLab/data/:/data/db/ #(2)
      - /vol/mongoVaSiLiLab/mongod.conf:/etc/mongod.conf
      - /vol/mongoVaSiLiLab/log/:/var/log/mongodb/
      - /vol/mongoVaSiLiLab/mongohome/:/home/mongodb/
    command: [ "-f", "/etc/mongod.conf" ]

volumes:
  mongodb_data_container:
  1. Customise the data according to your needs.
  2. Change the directories according to your system.

bindIp: 127.0.0.1 only accepts local connections

With this setting MongoDB is reachable only from the container itself, so an API running elsewhere cannot connect. Widen it to the interface the API reaches it on - and keep security.authorization enabled if you do.

mongod.conf
# for documentation of all options, see:
#   http://docs.mongodb.org/manual/reference/configuration-options/

# Where and how to store data.
storage:
  dbPath: /data/db

# where to write logging data.
systemLog:
  destination: file
  logAppend: true
  path: /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log

# network interfaces
net:
  port: 27017
  bindIp: 127.0.0.1 #(3)

# security
security.authorization : enabled

docs.title: Database API
docs.text:
Serves the scene, level and role definitions the VR client loads, and provides the logging endpoints that all tracking and experiment data is written through into MongoDB.

Previously referred to here as the Python Data Logger. It is available now, in the Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend monorepo under database-api/.

Full documentation

Endpoints, environment variables, authentication and the batched /logging/player payload are documented at Database API in the backend documentation.

docs.title: Port
docs.text: Defaults to 5000, configurable with the PORT environment variable.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint requires a shared secret header:

X-API-KEY: <value of X_API_KEY>

A wrong key loses the session silently

Logging failures do not interrupt an experiment. The session runs normally and records nothing. Verify data is arriving before a participant sits down.

docs.title: Unity
docs.text:
MetaDataLogger > http://ip:5000

Set the same API key in the Va.Si.Li API asset.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
The backend consists of two required services and a number of optional ones, depending on the scenario.

Service Purpose Ubiq Server Room and session state - avatars, transforms, ownership required Database API Scene definitions and the logging API, backed by MongoDB required VR Agent (vr-agent/) LLM agents for the Bots optional TTS/STT (tts-stt/) Speech-to-text and text-to-speech for the agents optional Speech (speech2text/) Whisper speech-to-text for voice input optional Chatbot (chatbot/) Older voice chatbot host optional

Which client setting points to which service is listed in Endpoints Configuration.

All of them live in the Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend monorepo.

Backend documentation

Each module - its endpoints, environment variables and deployment - is documented at texttechnologylab.github.io/Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend.

The pages in this section cover what the Unity client needs from each service; the backend docs cover the services themselves.

docs.title: Deploying the full stack
docs.text:
A standardised Docker Compose deployment exists as part of InterView, which brings the services up together - the Ubiq room server, the Database API, a Janus WebRTC gateway, an optional TURN relay and a web client - with versioned configuration instead of individually started containers.

Start here for a full deployment

The InterView Setup Guide walks through the whole stack step by step, including the prerequisites that are easy to miss: an external MongoDB, DNS records, firewall port ranges, and a TLS-terminating reverse proxy that correctly forwards WebSocket upgrades.

The stack was built for the FACES project, but nothing in it is FACES-specific apart from the web client - the same deployment serves any Va.Si.Li-Lab scenario that needs a room server and a logging backend.

docs.text:
The networking between multiple user is handled by Ubiq. (Documentation) (GitHub)

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
We use a slightly modified version of the official Ubiq. One reason for this is that the original was not equipped with a corresponding Docker file. The other reason is that we had to add some functions to the original Ubiq. Now there is also an official docker build variant, which is why we want to integrate ubiq directly in a new version.

The server lives in the Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend monorepo under Ubiq-server/.

git clone https://github.com/texttechnologylab/Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend.git
cd Va.Si.Li-Lab-backend/Ubiq-server
docker build -t ubiq .
docker run -d --restart unless-stopped -p 8009:8009 -p 8011:8011 ubiq

Configuration and full reference

Ports, the layered nconf configuration and the iceservers block are documented at Ubiq Server in the backend documentation.

Deployment overrides belong in config/local.json, which is not tracked - not in the committed config/default.json.

docs.title: Unity
docs.text: The client reads the server address from Ubiq Server (a Ubiq ConnectionDefinition) in Assets/Resources/VasiliEndpoints.asset. Create the file with Tools > Va.Si.Li > Create Endpoints Config. The VasiliServerConnection component on the RoomClient of the Social Network Scene prefab applies it at start-up. If the file is missing, the client falls back to 127.0.0.1:8009 and logs a warning.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text: The Ubiq server is also part of the combined InterView deployment stack, which starts it alongside the other backend services with restart policies and versioned configuration.

docs.title: General
docs.text: This documentation is based on the MkDocs-Material framework. It is written in Markdown and can be found in the Documentation/docs folder.

docs.title: Testing locally
docs.text:
With uv installed, no further setup is needed. From the repository root:

cd Documentation
uvx --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin --with mkdocs-glightbox mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Pages reload when you save.

Before opening a pull request, check that the docs build without warnings, as the CI does:

uvx --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin --with mkdocs-glightbox mkdocs build --strict

Without uv, install the same packages with pip (pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin mkdocs-glightbox) and run mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Adding a new page
docs.text: To add a new page, create a new markdown file in the Documentation/docs folder. Then insert the file path in the mkdocs.yml file under the nav section.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: The docs are built and published to GitHub Pages on every push to main and on every pull request, so a pull request shows up on the live site before it is merged.
